text.title: Freelancer Payment Chase Script Library Failure Modes
text.summary: 6 antipatterns observed when running a payment-chase ladder. Each pairs a symptom, a root cause, and a concrete fix keyed to a rule in 01-core-rules.xml.

antipattern.symptom: The firm rung lands on day 4 after the due date because the freelancer counted from the day they sent the invoice, or from the day they noticed; the client is offended by an invoice that was barely late.
antipattern.root-cause: Rung dates were set by calendar reminder rather than computed from the due date on the invoice.
antipattern.fix: Compute T from the invoice due date, record the three scheduled dates in the artefact, and block any rung from sending ahead of its clock.

antipattern.symptom: A rung threatens "a 5% weekly late fee" that appears in no contract; the client disputes the whole invoice and asks for the clause.
antipattern.root-cause: Consequence was written for effect, not lifted from the contract or a statute.
antipattern.fix: Remove any fee or leverage with no clause id or statutory basis; where a statute grants interest, quote the act and the rate.

antipattern.symptom: The first message after the due date mentions lawyers or collections; the client pays and never books again.
antipattern.root-cause: Frustration or a prior bad experience with another client wrote the tone; the ladder was skipped.
antipattern.fix: Rewrite rung one to the oversight assumption: invoice attached, one question, under 120 words, no consequences. Reserve legal language for the T+30 formal notice.

antipattern.symptom: A firm chase goes out the morning after payment cleared, or after the client emailed a specific complaint about the deliverable.
antipattern.root-cause: Rungs were pre-scheduled and nobody checked the ledger or inbox before sending.
antipattern.fix: Check payment status and dispute status immediately before every send; halt on either; route disputes to dispute handling and recompute balance on partial payment.

antipattern.symptom: Three rungs go to the project sponsor who has no authority over payments; finance never sees the invoice number.
antipattern.root-cause: Recipient list never widened beyond the day-to-day contact.
antipattern.fix: Add the accounts-payable or finance contact from rung two onward; keep the sponsor copied so the relationship context is preserved.

antipattern.symptom: The same client is 30 days late on every invoice for a year and is renewed on the same net-15 terms.
antipattern.root-cause: Sends and responses were never logged, so days-to-pay per client was never computed and renewal had no evidence to act on.
antipattern.fix: Log every send and response; compute days-to-pay per client; state the terms change (deposit, shorter terms, milestone billing) at renewal with the log as evidence.
